setup: Give each run a copy of the repository with its dependencies installed, and a home directory with the files below: beach.jpg in ~/Pictures, the photos in ./photos, and chroma-preset.json and garden.jpg in the current directory.

evals.prompt: Can you turn ~/Pictures/beach.jpg into one of those chroma puzzles for my 9 year old niece? Nothing too hard.
evals.expected_output: An easy puzzle ZIP outside the repository and a separate answer file, with a short report of where both are and how to make it again, without naming the real plates in the reply.
assertions: Makes the puzzle with the repository's CLI, and the puzzle ZIP exists
Writes the puzzle outside the repository checkout
Uses at most 4 real plates, and neither --occlusion nor --cipher
Writes an answer file that is not inside the puzzle
Checks that the real plates stack back into the image
Gives the seed or a saved config, and does not list the real plates in the reply

evals.prompt: puzzle night on friday!! make me hard puzzles from every jpg in ./photos, each one different, and keep whatever I'd need to regenerate them
evals.expected_output: One hard puzzle per photo, each with its own output path and answer file, the settings and seed kept for every one, and every run's warnings dealt with.
assertions: Makes one puzzle for every .jpg in ./photos, each to its own output path
Makes them hard: an --occlusion mode with a --decoy-intensity below 0.6, or --cipher
Keeps both the settings and the seed of every puzzle
Keeps the answer files apart from the puzzles that get handed out
Reads each run's warnings and acts on them

evals.prompt: I saved a preset in the app as chroma-preset.json. I want the same thing for garden.jpg but with 8 plates and cells, and last time it complained some plates were nearly empty
evals.expected_output: A puzzle from the preset with 8 plates in cells space and no nearly-empty plates, after dealing with the warning this image and preset produce.
assertions: Passes the preset with -c or --config, with 8 plates and the cells space as flags
Notices the nearly-empty warning the first run prints
The final puzzle has no nearly-empty real plate
Keeps the 8 plates and cells space, or explains why one of them had to change
Uses --force only on files it created itself
